Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — The reporter's complaint is a first-party Google Calendar onboarding card ("Welcome to your new Google Calendar" plus "Mobile apps" app-store badges), which is within the AdGuard Annoyances filters' scope, but the reported URL requires a signed-in Google account:⁠ it 302'd through accounts.google.com/ServiceLogin to the workspace.google.com marketing page, and the login-free calendar.google.com embed view — whose complete full-page capture was inspected and shows no such card — is not the reporter's page. Analysis only:⁠ the signed-in view is unreachable in this run, so no selector could be observed or validated.

## Executor and version

Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3

## Missing information

- No route to reach a reported page that sits behind an account sign-in wall: The reported URL https:⁠//calendar.google.com/calendar/u/0/r is served only to a signed-in Google account:⁠ in the locked browser_extension session it returned 302 to accounts.google.com/ServiceLogin and ended on https:⁠//workspace.google.com/intl/en-US/products/calendar/. The public embed view (calendar.google.com/calendar/embed?src=…holiday…) does load, but the reported "Welcome to your new Google Calendar" onboarding card is not present there, and no tool returns the DOM of the signed-in view. Neither the run instruction nor the linked guidance documents say how to handle a report whose page requires a login (no authenticated profile, no reporter DOM export), nor whether such a report should be handed to a maintainer. A cosmetic rule cannot be written or validated without the element's identifiers, so the run can only report the unreachable flow.

Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — The reported bottom cookie-consent panel on www⁠.raiffeisen.ru is a first-party `.CookieDialog` element that the repository already targets with `raiffeisen.ru##.CookieDialog` (AnnoyancesFilter/Cookies/sections/cookies_specific.txt), so no new rule is warranted. The locked AdGuard CLI environment reported that very rule as applied but injected no element-hiding CSS into the page's main document, so no candidate could be verified and the outcome is analysis-only.

## Still visible after the rule

- Bottom of TILE 1, below 'Как стать клиентом и открыть продукты банка' — Fixed rounded light-gray cookie consent panel overlaying the page; it contains the cookie-processing text and a 'Понятно' button.
- Bottom of viewport, overlaid across the lower page content — Fixed dark rounded cookie-consent panel visible at the bottom of the mobile viewport. It contains the consent text “Продолжая пользоваться сайтом, я соглашаюсь с условиями обработки файлов cookie” and a white “Понятно” button.

Reload the same page and repeat the same steps. > 9. Analysis-only findings, no verified change

## Reproduced symptom

Indeterminate — luluvido.com runs a first-party anti-adblock wall inside its player iframe:⁠ showADBOverlay()/showGuardOverlay() injects an obfuscated overlay, keeps it alive with a MutationObserver and destroys the jwplayer, triggered by the first-party just-detect-adblock library /js/jdadbl.js and matching the reporter's screenshot text exactly. The wall never renders in this filtered baseline (__adbDetected = false, no overlay, no difference between phases), so no candidate could be validated; the best unverified rule, carried for human review, is the domain-scoped scriptlet neutralizing the wall entry point.

## Candidate for review

`luluvido.com#%#//scriptlet('abort-on-property-read', 'showADBOverlay')`

BaseFilter/sections/antiadblock.txt

Not verified: apply_rule returned environmentExperiment 'inconclusive' with validationSkipped and errorKind 'baseline_symptom_absent':⁠ the wall is absent in every phase, so the candidate was never judged (2 attempts remained). In the player iframe https:⁠//luluvido.com/e/7gqji6oi42ql justDetectAdblock is defined, __adbDetected is false, no guard overlay exists and no stylesheet hides the bait, so this proxy environment never triggers the detector. A cosmetic hide could not replace it:⁠ the overlay classes are randomised per load (.a899302 then .a793512 on the same URL), it has no CSS display:⁠none (so the sibling family selector in BaseFilter/sections/antiadblock.txt:⁠4335 cannot match), the MutationObserver re-shows it, and showGuardOverlay removes the jwplayer. Blocking /js/jdadbl.js was rejected because the page then calls showADBOverlay() immediately.

comment.body:
Candidate rule proposed ## Reproduced symptom Reproduced — Arcade Punks serves an English anti-adblock gate ("Ads keep Arcade Punks running" / "AD BLOCKER DETECTED") built \~3 s after load by the page's own inline script, which locks scrolling and hides the page if the modal is hidden — so element hiding cannot work, as the reporter found. A scriptlet that aborts that inline script verified clean in the A/B/C experiment (gate gone, page intact, no residue), so the run proposes it for BaseFilter/sections/antiadblock.txt. ## Rule `arcadepunks.com#%#//scriptlet('abort-current-inline-script', 'document.createElement', 'Network or DNS blocker detected')` ## Executor and version Pinned prebuilt release v5.5.2.3 ## Policy rationale Not a German anti-adblock wall:⁠ the page and the gate are English, so the German-wall exclusion does not apply. Not the site's own advertising and not a paywall:⁠ the reported target is an anti-adblock gate injected over already-loaded article content, not an ad and not content access control. The report is an anti-adblock wall whose detector script was captured:⁠ the page's inline wall script was read from the DOM and shows the decoy-offsetHeight and pagead2 probe detection vectors that produce the gate. Filter policy allows blocking anti-adblock walls that aggressively insist on removing the ad blocker or effectively prevent using the website:⁠ the gate covers the full viewport, locks scrolling and hides the whole page if the modal is hidden. Not a scam/phishing page; the rule stops the gate and leaves the page content intact (verified). ## Place in the list [BaseFilter/sections/antiadblock.txt](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/20a879d17f81622e723e4eacb357a0a9b9406162/BaseFilter/sections/antiadblock.txt) Next to the site's existing rules, before [line 693](https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/blob/20a879d17f81622e723e4eacb357a0a9b9406162/BaseFilter/sections/antiadblock.txt#L693). ## Screenshots
